idea-plugin.name: JSON Canopy
idea-plugin.description:
JSON Canopy opens .json files as nested, filterable, editable tables instead of raw text, in an extra tab next to the built-in JSON editor.

Explore

  • Objects and arrays render as tables inside tables. An array of objects becomes one column per item, so you can compare entries at a glance.
  • Flip a table between horizontal and vertical orientation, and hide columns with the field selector.
  • Large arrays are paged, so big files stay responsive. Load more items when you need them.

Search

One search box, three ways to look at the results:

  • Matches: only what matched. A matching name shows with its value collapsed, a matching value shows under a dimmed name.
  • Path: every match with its hierarchy. A matching name shows its whole value, and the names above the match show the way to it.
  • Context: matches with their surroundings. All attributes of the containing object are shown, including sibling sub-trees.
  • Names only ignores values, for "give me every description" searches.
  • Matches are highlighted, names that are only there for structure or context are dimmed, and a line under the search box explains the active mode.

Collapse and expand

  • Every object and array has a ▾ button to collapse it, with or without a search. Collapsed nodes (including the ones a search leaves collapsed) show a chip you click to expand.
  • Shift+click applies to all related nodes at once, such as the same column in every row of an array.
  • The field selector closes with Esc or a click outside.

Edit in place

  • Change any value directly, with a type dropdown per value (string, number, boolean, null, object, array).
  • Add or remove object keys and array items with + and ×.
  • Edits go through the IDE, so undo and redo work.
  • Prefer text? Edit the whole document as raw JSON, or copy and download the result.

Fits your IDE

  • Light and dark themes follow the IDE theme automatically.
  • It is an additional tab. Schema validation and completion stay on the standard JSON tab, so this is a specialized view, not a replacement.

Source code and issues: github.com/OldPeasant/json-canopy
